subject: Biotechnology
title: CRISPR Diagnostics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on CRISPR Diagnostics.

hook.text: CRISPR is not just for editing — it detects diseases too. SHERLOCK and DETECTR find viruses in a drop of blood.

buildup.text: Cas13 binds target RNA and activates collateral cleavage — cutting reporter molecules that produce a signal.

discovery.text: The test works on a paper strip — one line means negative, two lines means positive, like a pregnancy test.

twist.text: CRISPR diagnostics detect attomolar concentrations — a single molecule in a microliter of fluid.

climax.text: Field-deployable CRISPR tests diagnosed Zika, Dengue, and SARS-CoV-2 — lab precision in a portable format.

punchline.text: From gene editor to disease detector — CRISPR does both.

quiz.question: How does SHERLOCK use CRISPR to detect diseases?
options: It edits viral genes to make them visible under a microscope
Cas13 binds target RNA and triggers collateral cleavage that produces a detectable signal
It inserts fluorescent genes into viruses to track them

details.summary: CRISPR-based diagnostics like SHERLOCK and DETECTR use Cas proteins to identify specific nucleic acid sequences with extraordinary sensitivity, enabling rapid point-of-care detection of viruses, cancer mutations, and antibiotic-resistant bacteria without expensive laboratory equipment.
details.whyItMatters: Rapid, accurate, inexpensive diagnostics are critical for pandemic response and healthcare in resource-limited settings. CRISPR diagnostics achieve laboratory-grade sensitivity on paper strips, potentially democratizing access to molecular
takeaways: SHERLOCK and DETECTR detect specific DNA or RNA sequences using Cas proteins
They achieve attomolar sensitivity comparable to PCR-based testing
Results appear on simple paper strips in under an hour without lab equipment

faq.question: How sensitive are CRISPR-based diagnostic tests?
faq.answer: SHERLOCK can detect single molecules of target RNA or DNA, achieving attomolar sensitivity comparable to gold-standard PCR. When combined with isothermal amplification, it detects Zika virus at concentrations as low as 2 attomolar. This sensitivity rivals the best laboratory tests.

faq.question: Could CRISPR diagnostics replace PCR testing?
faq.answer: For many applications, yes. CRISPR diagnostics offer comparable sensitivity without thermocyclers or trained technicians. They work at constant temperature, produce results in under an hour, and read out on paper strips. Cost per test can be under two dollars.
